paper_title: Derandomized Graph Product Results Using the Low Degree Long Code
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 3
statement: A similar derandomized “majority is stablest” result in the case of the noisy hypercube was proved by Barak et al. [2, Theorem 5.6] and they used the Meka-Zuckerman pseudorandom generators (PRGs) for polynomial threshold functions [14]. Kane and Meka [11] obtained a quantitative improvement over this derandomization by constructing an improved PRG for Lipschitz functions. Our setting is slightly more involved, (1) we have a two function version (ie., A and B) and (2) the underlying graph in K3 and the corresponding noise operator in the derandomized setting has not necessarily positive eigenvalues. Yet, we manage to show that a derandomization still holds in this case too (using the Kane-Meka PRG). We conjecture that our derandomization can be further improved to obtain d = O(log log 1/µ).
